infusion

/in-FYOO-zhun/ - the stress falls on FYOO · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Infusion means the introduction of one thing into another, such as money, energy, or flavor.

Opening the windows sent an infusion of pine-cold air through the stuffy cabin.

Example

By its third year the festival committee had gone stale: same booths, same banner, same shrinking crowd. Then the high school's robotics club asked for a table, and the infusion was immediate — night-market lighting rigged from kit parts, a drone lantern show, a ticket app the older members happily surrendered to. Attendance doubled, and the average age of a volunteer fell by thirty years.

Infusion is the exact word for what the club brought, because an infusion is the introduction of one thing into another — money, energy, or flavor — and the introduced thing spreads through the whole. An injection is quick and local; an infusion steeps, the way that new energy worked its way into every corner of the festival.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

injection: An injection is quick, forceful, and local — the added thing lands in one spot at one moment. An infusion is slower and spreads: what is introduced steeps through the whole and changes its overall character. If the boost stays where it entered, injection; if it seeps everywhere, infusion.

dose: A dose is a measured amount given deliberately, usually as medicine — its point is the exact quantity. An infusion cares about spread, not measurement: the introduced thing works through the whole it enters. A dose stays countable; an infusion becomes part of everything around it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

drain: what takes out as an infusion puts in

withdrawal: removing what was put in

Where it sits · how much the addition transforms the whole — splash → infusion → flood

splash vs. infusion: A splash is much milder than an infusion — a token amount, a little color or a little cash, gone without changing anything.

flood vs. infusion: A flood goes further than an infusion — an infusion spreads through the whole and improves it; a flood overwhelms the whole and replaces it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: into

Root — fus

Root — fus: poured (Latin fundere)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: the act of

Put it together

Put it together: In- (into) + fus- (poured) + -ion (the act of) = the act of pouring in. Latin infundere poured liquids; English lets anything pourable in — money, energy, flavor — so long as it spreads through whatever receives it.

Use the root in a new word: refund

Use the root in a new word: refund: A refund is money 'poured back' — fus- and fund- are the same Latin pour, and a refund reverses the direction of the flow.

Word Choice

neutral / journalistic

Infusion is the revival word: an infusion of cash, of energy, of young talent. An injection is faster and more local; a dose is measured medicine. Use infusion when the added thing spreads through the whole and changes its temper.
